title: A normal polynomial domain surjects onto every commutative ring
statement: For every commutative ring $A$, there exist a set $J$, a normal integral domain $P=\mathbb Z[x_j:j\in J]$ [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and a surjective ring homomorphism $P\to A$. The variables may be indexed by the underlying set of $A$, with each variable sent to the corresponding element of $A$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 030A (polynomial ring over a normal domain is normal), together with the standard free-polynomial evaluation presentation; the quotient reduction used in Huebner--Schmidt Theorem 6.3, printed p. 13.

proof_origin.place: counit (64--65), counit_surjective (75--76), counit_X (90--91), with the domain/UFD/integral-closed instances enumerated in mathlib_match.how; Mathlib leaf, no proof steps.

mathlib_match.how: One declaration per clause, with inferred instances (delivery-errors B8). Take J to be the underlying type of A and P = MvPolynomial A Z. The ring homomorphism is MvPolynomial.counit A (Mathlib/Algebra/MvPolynomial/Counit.lean:64--65), surjective by MvPolynomial.counit_surjective (:75--76), with X(a) mapped to a by MvPolynomial.counit_X (:90--91). The domain clause is the instance MvPolynomial.instIsDomainOfIsCancelAdd (Mathlib/Algebra/MvPolynomial/Basic.lean:203--204), instantiated at R=Z. Integral closedness is UniqueFactorizationMonoid.instIsIntegrallyClosed (Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/RationalRoot.lean:139--140), whose unique-factorization instance is MvPolynomial.uniqueFactorizationMonoid (Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/UniqueFactorization.lean:130--143) at D=Z; the integer UFD instance is inferred. Thus normal domain means exactly IsDomain P and IsIntegrallyClosed P, as def-weil-pbc-normal-ring specifies. All clauses specialize directly; no finiteness or nontriviality of A is required.
